OWNER is deliberately absent (ENTRA_MAPPABLE_ROLES in src/app-layer/schemas/entra-group-mapping.ts is `every Role except OWNER`). OWNER carries `admin.tenant_lifecycle` (suspend or close the club) and `admin.owner_management` (change who owns it); a mapping that granted it would make club ownership transferable by editing an Active Directory group, by directory administrators outside this application who have no way of knowing what the role means here.

The refusal is repeated four times: this Zod enum, `assertMappable` in the use case, the sync's OWNER-immunity check, and a CHECK constraint in migration P27. Sending `"OWNER"` to this API is rejected by the Zod enum FIRST, so the response is 400 with code `BAD_REQUEST` (not `ROLE_NOT_MAPPABLE`) — see the 400 response description.

EntraGroupMapping.description: One Entra group → role mapping, as produced by `toGroupMapping` in src/app/api/v1/_lib/dto.ts. Every property is always present; `aadGroupName` is nullable rather than omitted.

id.description: Server-generated identifier (Prisma `@default(cuid())`) — a cuid, NOT a UUID. Treat it as an opaque string.

aadGroupId.description: The Entra security-group object id. Always LOWER CASE here: the create schema lower-cases on the way in, so this can differ from the string the client sent (an admin pasting an upper-cased GUID from a portal gets it back lower-cased). Compare case-insensitively, or re-read this value after a write.

aadGroupName.description: Cached Microsoft Graph display name. Cosmetics only — the sync never matches on it, because a group can be renamed in the directory at any time and this copy would then be a lie that looks authoritative. Null when never supplied.

priority.description: Higher wins when a user is in several mapped groups. Admin-set, never derived from role seniority: a club may deliberately want a narrow group to beat a broad one ("everyone" → PLAYER at 0, "coaching staff" → COACH at 100).

createdAt.description: RFC 3339, UTC, with NO fractional seconds (`rfc3339()` strips the milliseconds `toISOString()` emits, because Swift's `.iso8601` decoding strategy rejects them).

updatedAt.description: RFC 3339, UTC, no fractional seconds. Maintained by Prisma `@updatedAt`.

EntraGroupMappingEnvelope.description: The v1 success envelope around a single mapping: `ok(data)` emits `{"data": <T>}`. There is no top-level bare object on any v1 route.

EntraGroupMappingListEnvelope.description: The list response. NOTE: this route calls `ok(array)`, not `page()` — `data` is a bare ARRAY, with no `items`/`nextCursor` object. Do not generate a paginated decoder for it.

data.description: Ordered by `priority` DESC, then `createdAt` ASC. Hard-capped server-side at 200 rows with no cursor and no indication of truncation — deliberate: a club with more mapped groups than that has a configuration problem, not a pagination problem.

EntraGroupMappingCreate.description: Request body for creating a mapping (`EntraGroupMappingCreateSchema`). Unknown properties are stripped, not rejected.

aadGroupId.description:
The Entra security-group OBJECT ID — a GUID, never a display name. Validated with Zod 4 `z.string().uuid()`, which is RFC 9562-strict: the version nibble must be 1–8 and the variant nibble 8/9/a/b (the nil and max UUIDs are also accepted). A display name here would silently never match any `groups` claim and the mapping would look configured while doing nothing, which is why this is validated rather than accepted as free text.

Accepted in any case and STORED LOWER-CASED; the response echoes the lower-cased form.

aadGroupName.description: Optional cached Graph display name. Trimmed first, then length-checked, so a whitespace-only string is a 400. Must be a string or omitted — explicit `null` is rejected (400). Omitted stores null.

priority.description: Optional; defaults to 0. Must be an integer in [0, 1000] — a float or a numeric string is a 400.

EntraGroupMappingUpdate.description:
Request body for a partial update (`EntraGroupMappingUpdateSchema`). At least one of the three properties must be present: an empty object is rejected with 400 ("At least one field must be provided") rather than returning 200 having changed nothing, because an empty PATCH is a client bug that would otherwise read as success.

`aadGroupId` is NOT updatable — it is absent from the update schema, so unknown keys are stripped and a body containing only `aadGroupId` parses to `{}` and fails the same 400. Re-point a group by deleting the mapping and creating a new one.

aadGroupName.description: Trimmed, then length-checked. There is NO way to clear a name back to null through this API: `null` is rejected by the schema, and an omitted property leaves the stored value untouched.

RealtimeTokenEnvelope.description: The success envelope produced by `ok(data)`. The payload is under `data`; nothing is returned at the top level.

RealtimeToken.description: A Centrifugo connection credential and where to spend it.

token.description: HS256 JWT, three base64url segments. Its claims are exactly `sub`, `iat` and `exp` — no channel grants, no role, no tenant.

expiresInSeconds.description: Lifetime of `token` in SECONDS from issuance (currently 900). This is a duration, not a timestamp. Refresh before it elapses: a minted token cannot be revoked, so this value is the revocation window.

url.description: The public Centrifugo WebSocket URL, from `NEXT_PUBLIC_CENTRIFUGO_URL`. NULL when that variable is unset on the server — the token is still minted and the response is still 200, so a client must handle null rather than assume a URL is always present.

CentrifugoSubscribeRequest.description: What Centrifugo POSTs to the subscribe proxy. `user` is a claim from the BROKER, not from the browser: Centrifugo derived it from the JWT this server signed, and the shared header secret is what makes it trustworthy. Additional properties are permitted and ignored.

user.description: The connecting user's id (a cuid). Marked required because Centrifugo always sends it; at runtime a missing, empty or non-string value is not a 4xx — it is answered HTTP 200 with the `403 forbidden` deny body, since every channel this server issues is personal and none is subscribable anonymously.

channel.description: The channel being joined. Recognised shapes: `conv:<cuid>`, `notif:<cuid>`, `presence:user:<cuid>`. Marked required because Centrifugo always sends it; a missing or unrecognised value is answered HTTP 200 with the `403 forbidden` deny body.

CentrifugoSubscribeResponse.description: Centrifugo's proxy decision. Exactly one of `result` or `error` is present; both arrive with HTTP status 200.

result.description: Always the empty object. This server attaches no subscription options (no info, data or expire_at).

CentrifugoSubscribeDeny.description: Subscription refused. The reason is logged server-side and never disclosed here — every refusal is byte-identical, so the response cannot be used to probe whether a conversation exists.

code.description: An INTEGER, unlike the string `code` used in this API's own error envelope. 403 for every refusal decision; 503 when `CENTRIFUGO_PROXY_SECRET` is unset on the server, in which case every request is refused.
Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, never on `message`.

message.description: Human-readable. Wording may change without notice.

requestId.description: Correlates with the server's logs. Present on errors produced by the route wrapper; ABSENT on a few written inline by handlers (the 401 from /auth/token, the 400 and 401 from /auth/refresh). Treat it as optional.

bundleId.description: The app's bundle identifier. A token is only valid for the topic it was issued to.

environment.description: SANDBOX for debug builds, PRODUCTION for TestFlight and the App Store. Getting this wrong is the usual cause of 'works in TestFlight, not in the App Store'.
